nodes.characterization_summary: Satellite peaks in XPS show Co^{3+} in Zn_{0.8}Co_{2.2}O_4 is in the intermediate spin (IS) (t_{2g}^{5}e_g^{1}) or high spin (HS) (t_{2g}^{4}e_g^{2}) state rather than low spin (LS) state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By comparing the satellite peaks in X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), they found that Co^{3+} in Zn_{0.8}Co_{2.2}O_4 was in the intermediate spin (IS) (t_{2g}^{5}e_g^{1}) or HS (t_{2g}^{4}e_g^{2}) state other than in the LS state.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES, XPS, and FTIR prove that the structure of ZnCo_2O_4 calcined at different temperatures was distorted spontaneously, leading to the change of spin state of Co^{3+}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Xu and coworkers used X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES), XPS, and Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) to prove that the structure of ZnCo_2O_4 calcined at different temperatures was distorted spontaneously, leading to the change of spin state of Co^{3+}

nodes.characterization_summary: Satellite peaks in XPS confirm HS-Co^{3+} in the surface of spinel cobalt oxide obtained by expanding the lattice through surface treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HS-Co^{3+} in the surface of spinel cobalt oxide was obtained by expanding the lattice through the surface treatment of cobalt carbonate, which was obtained by comparing the satellite peaks in XPS

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES and XPS analysis confirm that the (100) facet of LaCoO3 film contains more intermediate spin (IS) states than the (110) and (111) facets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By analyzing XANES and XPS, they confirmed that the (100) facet contained more IS states than the (110) and (111) facets

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized Co K-edge XANES spectra show Fe doping in LaCoO3 (LaCo_{0.90}Fe_{0.10}O3) leads to lattice distortion and spin state transition of Co^{3+}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Duan et al. found that the Fe doping in LaCoO3 (LaCo_{0.90}Fe_{0.10}O3) led to the lattice distortion and spin state transition of Co^{3+} as characterized by normalized Co K-edge XANES spectra.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS peaks comparison with other Co-containing compounds shows that neighboring Co_Ta increases the spin density of Co_HS active sites to an optimized value in M-SACs on TaS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By comparing XPS peaks with those of other Co-containing compounds, they found that the neighboring Co_Ta increased the spin density of Co_HS active sites to an optimized value, resulting in an optimal binding energy between Co_HS and O species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Comparing satellite peaks in XPS confirms HS-Co^{3+} in the surface of PE-z-Co_3O_4 obtained by expanding the lattice through surface treatment of cobalt carbonate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HS-Co^{3+} in the surface of spinel cobalt oxide was obtained by expanding the lattice through the surface treatment of cobalt carbonate, which was obtained by comparing the satellite peaks in XPS (Figure 4e,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Integral areas of the e_g peak to the t_{2g} peak of XPS spectra confirm spin state of Ni^{2+} tends to be HS in ultrathin NiSe2 nanosheets due to structure distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the spin state of Ni^{2+} tended to be HS in ultrathin NiSe2 and NiS nanosheets due to structure distortion, which was confirmed by the integral areas of the e_g peak to the t_{2g} peak of XPS spectra, and further confirmed by XANES.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES confirms spin state of Ni^{2+} tends to be HS in ultrathin NiSe2 nanosheets due to structure distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the spin state of Ni^{2+} tended to be HS in ultrathin NiSe2 and NiS nanosheets due to structure distortion, which was confirmed by the integral areas of the e_g peak to the t_{2g} peak of XPS spectra, and further confirmed by XANES.
